data.description:
## Context / Problem

`file_impact` today is a **two-valued** field: a list of `{path, reason}` entries, or empty.
Empty is overloaded — it means BOTH "the author forgot to declare the edit-set" AND "this
ticket genuinely changes no code" (a docs-only task, an operator/config action, a
coordination or research ticket). Because the two are indistinguishable, rebar has to treat
empty conservatively everywhere:

- `dependency_hashes` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:281) returns `{}` for an
  undeclared ticket, and `compute_validity` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:707) then
  falls back to **whole-HEAD freshness** — ANY commit in the repo invalidates the plan-review
  attestation and forces a re-review.
- `_inherited_child_impact` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:241) applies a **poison
  rule**: one non-closed child with empty `file_impact` collapses the whole container's drift
  scope to `{}`, so a single genuinely-no-code child drags its parent (and every sibling's
  careful declaration) back to whole-HEAD invalidation.
- `p9_file_impact_coverage` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py:267) nags a leaf that
  declares nothing, even when nothing is the truth.

The conservative behavior is CORRECT for "forgot"; it is pure churn for "genuinely none". The
fix is to make the distinction **explicit** — a tri-state code impact — so the gate can be
conservative about silence and precise about an explicit claim, and so the claim itself can be
reviewed for truthfulness.

## Approach

Introduce an explicit third state on the existing FILE_IMPACT event stream:
`code_impact ∈ {undeclared, paths, none}` plus a required `code_impact_reason` for `none`.

- `undeclared` (empty list, no declaration) — TODAY's behavior, unchanged: whole-HEAD
  fallback, container poison, P9 advisory.
- `paths` (non-empty `file_impact`) — TODAY's behavior, unchanged.
- `none` (empty list + explicit declaration) — NEW: the attestation's signed manifest records
  `code-scope: none`, so no code drift invalidates it; the child neither contributes to nor
  poisons a container's inherited drift scope; P9 passes; and a new plan-review criterion
  checks the claim is actually true against the plan.

The declaration is part of the **material fingerprint**, so flipping between the three states
invalidates the attestation and forces a re-review — an author cannot retroactively widen an
attestation's validity by claiming "no code changes" after signing.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] A ticket that explicitly declares no code changes keeps its plan-review attestation
      valid across unrelated commits (checked: sign an attestation for such a ticket, commit
      an unrelated file, `rebar review-plan <id> --status` still reports certified/valid).
- [ ] A ticket with EMPTY, undeclared `file_impact` still invalidates on any commit (checked:
      the same experiment on an undeclared ticket reports `stale-head`).
- [ ] A container whose non-closed children are a mix of path-declaring and explicitly
      no-code children inherits exactly the path-declaring children's union — the no-code
      child does not poison it (checked: unit test over `_inherited_child_impact`).
- [ ] A plan-review criterion fires when a ticket claims no code changes but its plan
      describes work that requires code changes (checked: criterion prompt + routing shipped,
      registered in the canonical set, and the generated criteria guide regenerated).
- [ ] Closing a ticket that declared no code changes but whose landed `rebar-ticket:` commit
      modified source is rejected with an actionable error (checked: close-gate test).
- [ ] Every state transition of the tri-state changes the material fingerprint (checked: unit
      test over `material_fingerprint`).

## Child decomposition

1. **S1 — data model + write/read surface**: the FILE_IMPACT event carries the declaration;
   reducer state, schemas, generated types, CLI, MCP, and library reads/writes.
2. **S2 — attestation scoping**: the declaration enters the material fingerprint; the signed
   manifest records `code-scope: none`; `compute_validity` skips the whole-HEAD fallback for
   an explicitly-scoped-none attestation.
3. **S3 — container roll-up**: `_inherited_child_impact` treats a declared-none child as
   neutral (contributes nothing, poisons nothing); a container whose live children are ALL
   declared-none is itself scope-none; P9 passes on an explicit declaration.
4. **S4 — review criterion**: a plan-review criterion that validates a no-code-changes claim
   against the plan text.
5. **S5 — close-gate consistency + docs**: reject a close whose landed commit contradicts the
   declaration; update the gate/model/author docs and regenerate the criteria guide.

Children 2, 3 and 4 depend on 1; 5 depends on all of them.
data.title: Explicit 'no code changes' declaration: tri-state code impact on file_impact
